packet.headline_seed: WHO declares Ebola outbreak in DR Congo an international emergency
packet.description_seed: The agency added that the outbreak, with around 246 cases and 80 deaths, does not meet the criteria of pandemic emergency.

what: WHO declares Ebola outbreak in DR Congo an international emergency

clean_source_blocks.text: The World Health Organization (WHO) has declared an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo a public health emergency of international concern. The agency said the outbreak in DR Congo's eastern Ituri province, which has seen around 246 suspected cases and 80 deaths reported, does not meet the criteria of a pandemic emergency. But it warned it could potentially be "a much larger outbreak" than what is currently being detected and reported, with significant risk of local and regional spread. The current strain of Ebola is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, the health agency said, for which there are no approved drugs or vaccines. Early symptoms include fever, muscle pain, fatigue, headache and sore throat, and are followed by vomiting, diarrhoea, a rash and bleeding.
The agency added that the outbreak, with around 246 cases and 80 deaths, does not meet the criteria of pandemic emergency.

An outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has been declared an international "public health emergency" by the World Health Organisation (WHO). The WHO reports there are 246 suspected cases and 80 unexplained deaths so far in the DRC's Ituri province in the remote east of the country, bordering Uganda and South Sudan. But the true figure could be even higher, as the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) reports 87 deaths and 336 suspected cases, with 13 formal diagnoses. Two cases have been confirmed in Uganda's capital Kampala, including one death, from people said to have travelled from the DRC. The body of the patient who died in Kampala was later transported back to the DRC, with the Ugandan health ministry announcing the cases were "imported" from its neighbour.

A laboratory has also confirmed an Ebola case in the eastern city of Goma, currently controlled by the M23 rebels, the AFP news agency reported on Sunday. The WHO said the ongoing security situation and humanitarian crisis in DR Congo, combined with high population mobility, the urban location of the hotspot, and the large number of informal healthcare facilities in the region increased the risk of spread. Countries bordering the DR Congo are considered high risk due to trade and travel. The WHO advised that DR Congo and Uganda establish emergency operation centres to monitor, trace, and implement infection-prevention measures. To minimise spread, the health agency said confirmed cases should be immediately isolated and treated until two Bundibugyo virus-specific tests conducted at least 48 hours apart are negative.

payload.title: WHO julisti Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan ebolaepidemian kansainväliseksi terveysuhaksi
payload.summary: Maailman terveysjärjestö WHO on julistanut Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan itäosassa leviävän ebolaepidemian kansainväliseksi kansanterveysuhaksi. Epidemia ei WHO:n mukaan täytä pandemiaksi luokiteltavan hätätilanteen kriteerejä.
payload.content:
Maailman terveysjärjestö WHO on julistanut Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan itäisessä Iturin maakunnassa leviävän ebolaepidemian kansainväliseksi kansanterveysuhaksi. WHO:n mukaan alueella on raportoitu noin 246 epäiltyä tartuntaa ja 80 kuolemaa, mutta järjestö ei pidä tilannetta pandemiaksi luokiteltavana hätätilanteena.

## Tartuntojen todellinen määrä voi olla suurempi

WHO varoittaa, että epidemia voi olla nykyisiä havaintoja ja ilmoituksia laajempi. Järjestön arvion mukaan paikallisen ja alueellisen leviämisen riski on merkittävä.

Afrikan tautikeskus Africa CDC on arvioinut lukuja vielä korkeammiksi: sen mukaan epäiltyjä tapauksia olisi 336 ja kuolemia 87. Lisäksi muodollisesti vahvistettuja tartuntoja olisi 13. Luvuissa on eroja, koska osa tapauksista on epäiltyjä ja osa varmistettuja, ja alueen olosuhteet vaikeuttavat seurantaa.

Ebolaepidemia koskee erityisesti Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan itäosia, joissa turvallisuustilanne ja humanitaarinen kriisi vaikeuttavat terveysviranomaisten työtä. WHO:n mukaan leviämisriskiä kasvattavat myös väestön suuri liikkuvuus, kaupunkimaiset tartuntapesäkkeet sekä alueen lukuisat epäviralliset terveydenhuollon toimijat.

## Uganda ja naapurimaat riskialueella

Ugandan pääkaupungissa Kampalassa on vahvistettu kaksi tapausta, joista toinen johti kuolemaan. Tapausten kerrotaan liittyneen henkilöihin, jotka olivat matkustaneet Kongon demokraattisesta tasavallasta. Ugandan terveysministeriö on kuvannut tapauksia maahan tuoduiksi tartunnoiksi.

Myös itäisessä Goman kaupungissa on raportoitu laboratoriossa vahvistettu ebolatapaus. Kaupunki on M23-kapinallisten hallinnassa, mikä lisää viranomaisten työn vaikeutta alueella.

WHO pitää Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan naapurimaita korkean riskin alueina kaupan ja matkustamisen vuoksi. Järjestö on kehottanut Kongon demokraattista tasavaltaa ja Ugandaa perustamaan hätätoimintakeskuksia, joiden tehtäviin kuuluvat tilanteen seuranta, tartuntaketjujen jäljittäminen ja tartuntojen ehkäisy.

Epidemian aiheuttaa Bundibugyo-virus, joka on yksi ebolaviruksen muodoista. WHO:n mukaan tätä virusmuotoa vastaan ei ole hyväksyttyjä lääkkeitä tai rokotteita. Varhaisia oireita voivat olla kuume, lihaskipu, väsymys, päänsärky ja kurkkukipu. Myöhemmin tautiin voi liittyä oksentelua, ripulia, ihottumaa ja verenvuotoa.

WHO:n mukaan vahvistetut tartunnat tulisi eristää ja hoitaa, kunnes kaksi vähintään 48 tunnin välein tehtyä Bundibugyo-viruskoetta on negatiivisia.

Ugandassa on vahvistettu kaksi maahan tuotua tapausta, ja naapurimaita pidetään korkean riskin alueina.
article.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketissa olleisiin WHO:ta, Africa CDC:tä, Ugandan viranomaisia ja AFP:n raportointia koskeviin tietoihin. Luokitus korjattu ulkomaanuutiseksi, koska aihe ei liity Suomen kotimaan uutisiin.
article.source_text:
The World Health Organization (WHO) has declared an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo a public health emergency of international concern. The agency said the outbreak in DR Congo's eastern Ituri province, which has seen around 246 suspected cases and 80 deaths reported, does not meet the criteria of a pandemic emergency. But it warned it could potentially be "a much larger outbreak" than what is currently being detected and reported, with significant risk of local and regional spread. The current strain of Ebola is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, the health agency said, for which there are no approved drugs or vaccines. Early symptoms include fever, muscle pain, fatigue, headache and sore throat, and are followed by vomiting, diarrhoea, a rash and bleeding.

The agency added that the outbreak, with around 246 cases and 80 deaths, does not meet the criteria of pandemic emergency.

An outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has been declared an international "public health emergency" by the World Health Organisation (WHO). The WHO reports there are 246 suspected cases and 80 unexplained deaths so far in the DRC's Ituri province in the remote east of the country, bordering Uganda and South Sudan. But the true figure could be even higher, as the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) reports 87 deaths and 336 suspected cases, with 13 formal diagnoses. Two cases have been confirmed in Uganda's capital Kampala, including one death, from people said to have travelled from the DRC. The body of the patient who died in Kampala was later transported back to the DRC, with the Ugandan health ministry announcing the cases were "imported" from its neighbour.

A laboratory has also confirmed an Ebola case in the eastern city of Goma, currently controlled by the M23 rebels, the AFP news agency reported on Sunday. The WHO said the ongoing security situation and humanitarian crisis in DR Congo, combined with high population mobility, the urban location of the hotspot, and the large number of informal healthcare facilities in the region increased the risk of spread. Countries bordering the DR Congo are considered high risk due to trade and travel. The WHO advised that DR Congo and Uganda establish emergency operation centres to monitor, trace, and implement infection-prevention measures. To minimise spread, the health agency said confirmed cases should be immediately isolated and treated until two Bundibugyo virus-specific tests conducted at least 48 hours apart are negative.
